title: Grateful Dead Live at Reed's Ranch on 1969-07-03
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Samplitude Pro X Suite -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a rare early‑summer ’69 set with Jerry’s fledgling pedal steel, standout renditions of Green Green Grass of Home, Morning Dew and a sublime He Was a Friend of Mine.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that generally sounds great, though the first few minutes show some equipment wobble. Musically the show is a fascinating snapshot of the Dead experimenting with country‑rock, highlighted by Jerry’s pedal steel on Green Green Grass of Home and an epic 14‑minute He Was a Friend of Mine, while a few numbers like Hard to Handle feel sloppy.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show highly (5★) and praise its unique material; recording is praised as good with minor technical glitches, yielding an overall strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced sound; a brief equipment issue/waver in the opening minutes and some pitch tuning cuts noted, but overall the set sounds great.

standout_songs: He Was a Friend of Mine
Sitting on Top of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: One long early‑morning set built around Jerry’s new pedal steel, moving through country‑rock numbers and folk blues; experimental but surprisingly cohesive despite a few rough edges.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal steel is described as ‘interesting’ and a bit raw, yet adds a unique flavor; his guitar tone and vocal work on Morning Dew are praised.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s rendition of Green Green Grass of Home is highlighted as sweet; his southern‑accented delivery on Me & My Uncle is noted.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers are called ‘frantic’ and provide a driving pulse, though some cues slip on Hard to Handle.
